baseline.charter: Full-Lifecycle Engineering of Cybersecurity-Integrated Operational Technology (OT) Systems and Network Infrastructure in AI Data Centers — Revision 3.5, 19 September 2026
baseline.portfolio: Portfolio Architecture and Evidence Plan — Version 2.5
baseline.track_1: Curriculum MUDT — Revision 8 is referenced by the baseline but was not supplied for this implementation. Existing CCNA app and accepted Track 1 foundations are reused, not inferred completed.
baseline.scope: Near term D4–D7: networks, IT hardware, OT/controls and cybersecurity. D4, D6 and D7 are principal specialisations; D5 is mandatory and integral with evidence-based engineering judgment. D2/D3 foundations and integration are required now; full power/cooling engineering is a separate long-term D2–D7 gate.
exclusions: D1 civil, structural and architectural engineering is excluded from both horizons; retain external interface constraints only.
A separate cloud/workload-platform or AI-model engineering specialisation is not added.
No course, quiz, badge or app progress record confers production authority, professional competence or complete provider certification coverage.

architecture.primary_navigation: Subject overviews and target topic stages; full course structure remains under development
architecture.secondary_navigation: Certificate routes reuse the same lessons and practice
architecture.reason: Charter outcomes and certificate objectives require detailed course, module, chapter and lesson teaching. Shared concepts can be reused, but platform-specific implementation, diagnosis, recovery and independent assessment need their own instruction and evidence. The current overview links do not supply that depth.
architecture.weighting: D4/D6/D7 require sustained specialist depth that the current overview prototype has not delivered. D5 remains compulsory. Equal counts of overview lessons do not mean equal learning requirements or adequate coverage.
architecture.numbering_rule: D1–D7 domains, course Items 1–65, NET/HW/OT/SEC/CN outcomes, app lesson IDs, work packages and Releases 0–5 retain separate identities.

levels.title: Foundation target stage — understand and verify
levels.purpose: Explain systems, units, dependencies, controls, hardware and baseline security; begin safe hands-on work and simple recovery early.
levels.exit_gate: Complete prerequisite learning and knowledge checks, explain a worked example without the solution, and demonstrate a small bounded practical task at its declared evidence level. Reading and quiz completion alone represent knowledge progress.

levels.title: Applied target stage — implement and diagnose
levels.purpose: Use supported platforms to build, commission, test, operate, change and restore each required branch. Teach before guided practice; retain independent tasks and raw evidence.
levels.exit_gate: Demonstrate the mapped outcome against predefined criteria, including normal and fault behaviour, diagnosis, change/rollback and restoration; record source versions and access limitations.

levels.title: Advanced target stage — justify, assure and integrate
levels.purpose: Resolve ambiguous cross-domain faults, quantify constraints and uncertainty, validate automation, make acceptance decisions and prove repeated lifecycle performance. Advanced status increases difficulty and independence; it does not postpone any lifecycle responsibility.
levels.exit_gate: Independent review of all required outcome evidence and cumulative release gates, domain operating campaigns, physical work, trusted recovery, measured improvement and bounded claims. Separate exam readiness and field/production decisions remain open until evidenced.

outcomes.title: Physical media, optics and telecommunications
outcomes.scope: Engineer copper/fibre paths, racks/patching, connector polarity, transceiver compatibility, optical budgets, breakout, reach, error counters, capacity and physical diversity. Include carrier demarcation and equipment-management paths. Distinguish configured link rate from measured delivery and two circuits from physically independent routes.
outcomes.teaching_requirements: Reuse CCNA/DCCOR; add T-NET-01 and model-specific guided optics/cabling instruction T-LAB-01.
outcomes.practical_requirement: Produce a cable/optics schedule and loss-budget design; install and verify a real link; diagnose a safe mispatch or degraded link; retain inspection/test results and corrected as-builts. Emulation cannot close physical-media evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Produce a cable/optics schedule and loss-budget design; install and verify a real link; diagnose a safe mispatch or degraded link; retain inspection/test results and corrected as-builts.
Emulation cannot close physical-media evidence.

outcomes.title: Enterprise and campus routing/switching
outcomes.scope: Design dual-stack enterprise/campus networks, hierarchical topology, VLANs/VRFs, STP or routed access, gateway redundancy, OSPF/BGP policy, multicast, QoS and shared infrastructure services. Derive scale, convergence, isolation and maintainability requirements; compare planned behaviour with device and application state.
outcomes.teaching_requirements: T-NET-01 ENCOR; T-NET-02 ENARSI; reuse CCNA and existing packet-analysis teaching.
outcomes.practical_requirement: Build a routed campus environment; test IPv4/IPv6 service paths, isolation, link/device failure and a planned maintenance state. Diagnose routing/policy faults, roll back a change and prove restored service.
acceptance_criteria: Build a routed campus environment; test IPv4/IPv6 service paths, isolation, link/device failure and a planned maintenance state.

outcomes.title: Data-center networks and interconnection
outcomes.scope: Engineer leaf–spine underlays/overlays, ECMP, BGP EVPN/VXLAN, ACI, multi-tenant isolation, management connectivity, east–west/north–south flows and data-center interconnection. Assess MTU, congestion, oversubscription, control-plane dependencies and upgrade domains without conflating every vendor implementation.
outcomes.teaching_requirements: Existing full DCCOR, DCACI, DCID, DCIT and DCNAUTO assignments; platform-specific demonstrations.
outcomes.practical_requirement: Retain a requirements-led design and executable configuration; validate tenant paths and denial, MTU, failure/maintenance behaviour, migration and rollback. Independently assess ACI and EVPN/VXLAN outcomes where mechanisms differ.
acceptance_criteria: Retain a requirements-led design and executable configuration; validate tenant paths and denial, MTU, failure/maintenance behaviour, migration and rollback.

outcomes.title: PoPs, WAN and Internet edge
outcomes.scope: Engineer external connectivity, transit/peering concepts, eBGP policy, route filtering, maximum-prefix protection, route-origin validation, redundancy, DCI/WAN transport and carrier handoff. Include DNS reachability, asymmetric routing, edge security, provider escalation and routing-change blast radius.
outcomes.teaching_requirements: T-NET-02; T-LAB-02 instructor-led PoP/edge policy and route-origin-validation exercise; supported platform references.
outcomes.practical_requirement: Use an isolated multi-AS topology to test allowed/rejected advertisements, a route leak, upstream loss and policy rollback. Document provider boundaries and recovery. No public route advertisement or claimed live peering authority.
acceptance_criteria: Use an isolated multi-AS topology to test allowed/rejected advertisements, a route leak, upstream loss and policy rollback.

outcomes.title: Cloud and hybrid network connectivity
outcomes.scope: Engineer the network boundary to externally hosted services: address planning, routes, private connectivity, IPsec, SD-WAN, DNS, identity dependencies, MTU, failure and observability. Cloud services are endpoints or dependencies; this is network engineering, not a separate cloud-platform or workload-orchestration specialization.
outcomes.teaching_requirements: T-NET-03 bounded ENCC connectivity lessons; reuse Track 1 cloud foundations and existing VPN teaching.
outcomes.practical_requirement: Connect controlled on-premises and remote/cloud network segments, test routing and segmentation, tunnel/provider-path loss, DNS failure and rollback. Identify any emulated cloud boundary and do not infer production cloud operation.
acceptance_criteria: Connect controlled on-premises and remote/cloud network segments, test routing and segmentation, tunnel/provider-path loss, DNS failure and rollback.

outcomes.title: Wireless engineering and network admission
outcomes.scope: Cover RF fundamentals, coverage/capacity, surveys, AP/controller deployment, roaming, authentication, 802.1X, RADIUS/TACACS+, certificates and NAC policy. Include guest, managed and exceptional devices, controller loss and credential-service outages. Do not assume wireless is acceptable for every control function.

outcomes.practical_requirement: Perform a bounded real RF survey and deploy an authorised WLAN; test admission/rejection, roaming, certificate expiry/revocation and controller/AAA failure. Keep RF measurements separate from simulated configuration evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Perform a bounded real RF survey and deploy an authorised WLAN; test admission/rejection, roaming, certificate expiry/revocation and controller/AAA failure.

outcomes.title: Storage networking
outcomes.scope: Engineer Fibre Channel/SAN and IP storage paths, zoning, host/target access, multipathing, link/fabric independence, bandwidth/latency and congestion. Address iSCSI, NVMe-oF and relevant FCoE/DCB mechanisms; connect transport behaviour to storage availability, integrity and recovery rather than claiming success from link state.

outcomes.practical_requirement: Configure host-to-storage paths and isolation; test authorised I/O, rejected access, a path failure and restoration with data-integrity checks. Separate FC, IP and emulated evidence and retain hardware-access gaps.
acceptance_criteria: Configure host-to-storage paths and isolation; test authorised I/O, rejected access, a path failure and restoration with data-integrity checks.

outcomes.scope: Own inventory, approved designs/configurations, firmware, backups, access, telemetry, alerts, capacity, spares, changes, troubleshooting and service recovery. outcomes.scope: Understand CPU/GPU, memory/ECC, NUMA, PCIe lanes, NIC/HBA/DPU, local/shared storage, controller/cache, media endurance, firmware compatibility and replaceable components. outcomes.scope: Install and maintain Linux/Windows, drivers, management agents, controlled virtualisation and essential identity, DNS, time, storage, database and backup services used by the installation. releases.gate: Every claim links to a requirement; each test has an ID, environment, method and predefined acceptance criteria. Versioned evidence can be reviewed and reproduced; publication boundaries are controlled. Governance alone proves no technical capability.

releases.title: OT Systems, IT Hardware and Data-Center Lifecycle Ownership
releases.gate: Demonstrate the required physical function through instrumentation, controller, logic, supervisory system and operator decision, including maintenance, diagnosis and restoration. Real managed server/storage installation and safe sensing/actuation are required; software demonstrations alone cannot close physical outcomes.

releases.title: Network and Telecommunications Engineering
releases.gate: Accept each declared controls, campus, edge, wireless, hybrid, DC/storage and AI network branch against its own requirements and application-level tests, with maintenance, diagnosis and recovery. IP reachability alone is insufficient.

releases.title: OT, Network and Infrastructure IT Cybersecurity
releases.gate: Trace attack surface and authority through protection, detection, containment, eradication and trusted functional recovery. Restore function and remove malicious authority; test OT, network and infrastructure-IT boundaries separately.

releases.title: Operations and Lifecycle Management
releases.gate: Provide sufficient normal operating cycles, maintenance, changes, failed or rolled-back change, diagnosed faults, incidents, restoration and measured improvement. Acceptance is event- and evidence-based; elapsed study time does not pass the release.

releases.title: Automation, Modelling, and Assurance
releases.gate: Demonstrate repeatability, visible failure and authority boundaries, rollback/override/fallback, rejection of unsafe or invalid actions, model validation and uncertainty, and at least one measured operational improvement.

practical_cases.title: Physical-to-logical discrepancy
practical_cases.assignment: Introduce inconsistency among design, wiring, sensor placement, point mapping, control logic, HMI, and actual behaviour. Diagnose, correct, recommission, and update records.
practical_cases.status: Required practical assignment; not completed by an interactive quiz

practical_cases.title: Integrated commissioning
practical_cases.assignment: Commission the complete path from physical process through sensor, I/O, controller, logic, network, supervisory platform, historian, and operator decision.
practical_cases.status: Required practical assignment; not completed by an interactive quiz

practical_cases.title: Planned maintenance under reduced redundancy
practical_cases.assignment: Maintain a pump, controller, server, switch, firewall, or power path while proving remaining capacity, independence, risk controls, rollback, and restoration.
practical_cases.status: Required practical assignment; not completed by an interactive quiz

practical_cases.title: Cross-domain degradation
practical_cases.assignment: Distinguish physical, instrumentation, control, host, protocol, network, database, application, and display causes using measured evidence and competing hypotheses.
practical_cases.status: Required practical assignment; not completed by an interactive quiz

practical_cases.title: Reachability without application success
practical_cases.assignment: Keep IP connectivity operating while breaking a protocol, certificate, point mapping, time source, firewall state, translation, or session; prove the application or process failure.
practical_cases.status: Required practical assignment; not completed by an interactive quiz

practical_cases.title: Controlled infrastructure change and rollback
practical_cases.assignment: Execute a routing, firewall, firmware, certificate, remote-access, or configuration change with approval, backup, validation, failure detection, rollback, and final state verification.
practical_cases.status: Required practical assignment; not completed by an interactive quiz

practical_cases.title: Compromised engineering or vendor access
practical_cases.assignment: Exercise stolen or excessive authority, unauthorised configuration, malicious project download, or cross-zone movement; detect, contain, revoke, eradicate, and preserve required safe operation.
practical_cases.status: Required practical assignment; not completed by an interactive quiz

practical_cases.title: Trusted recovery
practical_cases.assignment: Recover a controller project, engineering workstation, control server, firewall, identity service, historian, or backup service; restore function, authority, configuration, measurements, policy, and trust.
practical_cases.status: Required practical assignment; not completed by an interactive quiz

practical_cases.title: Performance or efficiency optimisation
practical_cases.assignment: Establish a baseline, change a justified operating or control parameter, measure benefit and trade-offs, preserve constraints, and retain or reverse the change based on evidence.
practical_cases.status: Required practical assignment; not completed by an interactive quiz

practical_cases.title: Capacity and integration decision
practical_cases.assignment: Approve, reject, or conditionally approve a new AI load, controller, network segment, or cooling demand using power, cooling, controls, network, security, maintenance, and recovery evidence.
practical_cases.status: Required practical assignment; not completed by an interactive quiz

practical_cases.title: Server/storage installation and acceptance
practical_cases.assignment: Select and install physical hardware; commission BMC/firmware/boot and storage; run diagnostics and synthetic integrity/performance checks; establish approved baseline and real facility/network dependencies. Review both a correct and a flawed proposed configuration/installation method; explain the disposition and retain correction/retest and justified acceptance.
practical_cases.status: Required practical assignment; not completed by an interactive quiz

practical_cases.title: Hardware fault, repair and return to service
practical_cases.assignment: Identify a bounded hardware degradation, execute a real authorised FRU replacement, restore firmware/settings/service as needed, validate the result and reconcile maintenance/inventory records. Challenge an unsupported replacement diagnosis or repair method, justify the actual correction and return-to-service decision, and define recurrence checks.
practical_cases.status: Required practical assignment; not completed by an interactive quiz

practical_cases.title: Storage loss, rebuild and secure retirement
practical_cases.assignment: Exercise an authorised storage-path/media failure, evaluate reduced redundancy, restore independent data, then sanitise separate sacrificial media and retain identity/custody/validation records.
practical_cases.status: Required practical assignment; not completed by an interactive quiz

practical_cases.title: Enterprise/edge/wireless service continuity
practical_cases.assignment: Demonstrate separate campus, multi-AS edge and wireless/NAC functions; inject policy/AAA/path faults; diagnose, contain, roll back and restore without claiming simulated RF or live carrier experience.
practical_cases.status: Required practical assignment; not completed by an interactive quiz

practical_cases.title: AI/storage fabric diagnosis and recovery
practical_cases.assignment: Demonstrate representative supported fabric paths; diagnose congestion or link/partition error; verify restored service and isolation with hardware/fidelity limitations stated.
practical_cases.status: Required practical assignment; not completed by an interactive quiz

practical_cases.title: Compromised hardware-management authority
practical_cases.assignment: In an isolated authorised range, exercise a BMC/management credential or configuration compromise; preserve evidence, revoke authority, restore an approved baseline and prove management and dependent service trust. Do not inject unsafe firmware.
practical_cases.status: Required practical assignment; not completed by an interactive quiz

requirements: Repeated normal checks over multiple operating cycles and applicable modes
An alarm or abnormal condition, with useful monitoring and escalation
Preventive, condition-based or corrective maintenance with real work and post-work checks
A reviewed planned change with approved baseline and backup
A failed or rolled-back change and final state validation
A diagnosed fault with competing hypotheses and raw evidence
Security validation and an applicable incident exercise
Restoration with functional and administrative-trust validation
Measured improvement with before/after evidence and revised design or runbooks
operating_campaign.acceptance: Required for each domain and each declared network branch. Cross-domain reuse is allowed only when each requirement has its own test/evidence link. Neither calendar duration nor repeated task count substitutes for sufficient event evidence.

rules: Design intent, configured state, observed digital behaviour and physical outcome are separate evidence.
Reachability does not prove application delivery or physical success.
Authenticated telemetry does not establish sensor correctness.
Redundancy does not establish independent failure paths.
Technical competence does not grant authority.
Self-reported notes and app lesson completion are not independent portfolio acceptance.
physical_minimum: Real managed server/storage installation and authorised FRU replacement
Supported storage configuration, integrity check and independent restore with synthetic data
Real cabling/optical measurements and RF work for the corresponding claims
Recorded access for every claimed advanced accelerator/fabric/timing outcome

sufficiency.verdict: The app supplies original teaching and assessment across the planned credential pathways and broader engineering outcomes. Its course inventory and source mappings make that support inspectable. Completion of the intended professional identity also requires the retained vendor and physical work, sustained operating campaigns, accepted portfolio evidence and current provider requirements; application progress alone cannot establish it.
supported_claims: All 40 mandatory domain outcomes and eight controls-network requirements are retained in a traceability register.
Original courses have modules, teaching chapters, worked and guided practice, objective-linked assessment and independent tasks.
Each credential-related bank has at least 500 questions; CCNP includes all five retained courses and over 1,000 questions. ISA Expert is an integration milestone bank.
Additional network, hardware and controls teaching preserves requirements beyond the planned examinations.
The programme retains all nine lifecycle responsibilities, six cumulative releases and 16 practical case assignments.
completion_requires: Complete the authored instruction and assessments, review the published scope mappings and course-specific limits, and close any remaining provider or platform requirements with current instruction and independent practice.
Complete or demonstrate assessed equivalence for the named teaching and every unresolved targeted lesson.
Obtain supported vendor software, instructors, lab rights and the required physical equipment/access.
Complete independent practical work for all 48 outcomes and meet each work-package criterion.
Accept Releases 0–5 using operating history, defects/retests, incident/trusted recovery, measured improvement and independent review.
Verify the current full provider blueprint, eligibility and examination requirements separately for each planned credential.
Maintain honest distinctions among analytical, simulation, emulation, vendor simulation, physical laboratory, supervised field and production evidence.
not_established: Independent validation of complete proprietary provider scope, examination readiness or psychometric reliability of the original bank
Current competence, production operating experience, field authority, statutory or professional qualification
Complete vendor training content, complete official exam question banks or a guaranteed certification pass
Independent external review or acceptance of the learner’s work
Long-term D2/D3 engineering capability or firm-delivery readiness
Track 1 completion, because its current document and learner evidence were not supplied
sufficiency.long_term_hand_off: Add reviewed D2 power and D3 mechanical/cooling prerequisite, teaching, supervised practice and evidence routes across the same nine lifecycle responsibilities. Keep D1 excluded. Near-term controls, EPMS, BMS and modelling evidence cannot be relabelled as specialist power/cooling engineering ownership.
sufficiency.source_ref: Charter Rev3.5 §§2,4.4,6; Curriculum Rev14 §§08–12; Portfolio v2.5 §§16,21–22

delivery_status.requirements_mapping: All 48 mandatory outcomes are retained with assignments, practical criteria and supporting course links in the generated crosswalk.
delivery_status.detailed_teaching: Original credential courses and network, hardware and controls engineering extensions; inspect the generated inventory and each source baseline.
delivery_status.assessment_coverage: At least 500 original questions per credential-related bank, objective diagnostics and explained feedback. Provider equivalence and psychometric validity are not established by these counts.
delivery_status.stage_meaning: Foundation, Applied and Advanced describe increasing target difficulty and independence. Exit gates require evidence, not a title.
delivery_status.course_completion: Course study checkpoints require their authored question bank and study acknowledgement; they do not award credentials or practical acceptance.
